answer: Because the horizon index resolves every citation against the relic checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the terrace audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 78 aliases hence pays the authoring cost 78 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 5 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. That is 13 dollars per alias. What costs nothing to type costs plenty to act out.
